description: A stereo crossfader that swaps its two inputs between its two outputs, usable as a panner, a crossfader or a voltage-controlled amplifier

params.text: Sets the crossfade position reached with no CV patched, 0V to 5V; fully anticlockwise sends IN X to OUT 1 and IN Y to OUT 2, fully clockwise swaps them over
Scales the CV input before it is added to the INITIAL knob, from -1 to 1, so the CV can be turned round as well as turned down
Scales IN X before the crossfade, passing nothing fully anticlockwise and the whole input fully clockwise
Scales IN Y before the crossfade, passing nothing fully anticlockwise and the whole input fully clockwise

inputs.text: The signal that reaches OUT 1 with the crossfade fully anticlockwise and OUT 2 with it fully clockwise
The signal that reaches OUT 2 with the crossfade fully anticlockwise and OUT 1 with it fully clockwise
Shifts the crossfade: it is multiplied by the CV knob, added to the INITIAL knob, and the total clamped to 0V to 5V

outputs.text: A straight-line crossfade between the two inputs, all of IN X at one end of the control range and all of IN Y at the other
A straight-line crossfade between the two inputs, all of IN Y at one end of the control range and all of IN X at the other

notes: the INITIAL knob comes up in the middle of its range, so one signal patched to IN X arrives at half level on both outputs until the knob or the CV moves it.
the crossfade is linear rather than constant power, so at the middle each output carries half of each input.

inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
